newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Macquarie's Hannes to face trial.
newsitem.headline: Macquarie's Hannes to face trial.

text.p: A corporate finance executive at Macquarie Bank Ltd, Simon Hannes, would have to face trial on insider trading charges, magistrate Deborah Sweeney ruled on Tuesday.

In final submissions to a committal hearing against Hannes, the court was told he had learned from a colleague last July that transport firm TNT had been valued at between A$2.00 and just over A$3.00.
Dutch group Koninklijke PTT Nederland later made a successful A$2.45 per share bid for TNT.
The court was also told that Macquarie's corporate advisory unit valued shares in TNT at between A$2.35 and A$3.27 in the lead-up to the takeover bid.
Macquarie advised TNT during the agreed takeover.
The insider trading charges were brought by the Australian Securities Commssion. The charges carry a penalty of up to five years in jail.
Hannes, appearing relaxed and confident in rimless glasses, a dark suit and a spotted tie, told the court he had reserved his defence for a trial expected next year.
He declined to make any further statements to the court.
Hannes, posing as Mark Booth, is alleged to have bought about A$90,000 worth of A$2 TNT call options on September 17 and 18, before the October 2 announcement of the agreed takeover bid.
The exercise of the options would have made "Booth" a profit of about A$2 million.
The prosecution submitted that although Hannes was on leave and had not worked on the TNT advisory deal known as Project Tennis, he did receive direct information about the proposed takeover.
Hannes was alleged to have spoken to a Macquarie Bank employee working on Project Tennis in the week starting July 15 and asked what valuation range Macquarie had put on TNT.
When told the range of from about A$2 a share to above A$3, Hannes is alleged to said: "That sounds like a very high number. Do you really believe that?"
